current.title: Why gold fell about 30% from the January 2026 record
points: A blow-off top: gold ran to a record on 29 January 2026 after a near-vertical rally, then fell about a quarter by mid-year as ETF investors sold.
Rates went the wrong way for gold: the Fed raised rates a quarter point in September, the US 10-year yield went above 5% in October, and Fed speakers in November kept a December hike on the table.
A firm dollar: a 1% rise in the dollar index has gone with roughly a 1% fall in dollar gold since 2001.

Liquidation in the 16-20 November sell-off: an AI-led stock rout pushed funds to sell gold with equities to raise cash; gold fell about 9% in the week, its worst in eight months, to a 14-month low near $3,515.
Central-bank buying slowed at the higher prices, removing part of the floor that had held since 2022.
current.holding_up: Central banks still bought on dips (321 t in Jul-Sep 2026), the rupee kept weakening, which cushions gold in rupees, and Middle East tensions keep a safe-haven bid in the background.
current.sources: Reuters and Kitco, 20 Nov 2026; Newsweek, 20 Nov 2026; World Gold Council Q3 2026; earlier Gold Desk pages (6-7 Nov 2026).

2008.cause: Global financial crisis: funds sold everything for cash and the dollar surged.
2008.back: Fed cut to near zero and began QE; gold made new highs by 2009.

2009.cause: Pause after the 2008-09 rebound; a firmer dollar and rupee.
2009.back: Euro debt worries and loose money revived buying.

2012.cause: Euro crisis eased, the US recovery firmed and the Fed signalled the end of QE (the 2013 taper scare); ETFs dumped gold in the April 2013 crash.
2012.back: Took until 2019: Fed rate cuts, negative bond yields abroad and steady central-bank buying.

2013.cause: Taper scare and record ETF outflows.

2020-03.cause: COVID dash for cash: gold was sold with everything else.
2020-03.back: Unlimited Fed QE and zero rates; recovered within two weeks.

2020-08.cause: Vaccines and reopening lifted real yields from record lows and pulled money back into stocks.
2020-08.back: Record central-bank buying after the 2022 Russia sanctions, then the March 2023 US bank failures.

2025-10.cause: Profit-taking after a stretched record run.
2025-10.back: Central-bank and ETF buying resumed; new highs by December 2025.

2026.cause: See above: blow-off top, Fed hikes, 5% yields, firm dollar, AI-rout liquidation.
